title: Dropbox API Setup Guide: Access, Limits and Errors
summary: Dropbox API endpoints let you read, write, share and manage content. This guide covers access setup, rate limits and error handling.
body_markdown:
## Make a first working Dropbox API request


Both first calls use the same bearer token but different hosts and different places for their parameters, and that split's the part the headers documentation leaves you to infer.


When an upload returns a 400, the usual cause is parameters put in the body when they belonged in a header, or the reverse. Whoever's on call will find it there.


` /2/files/list_folder` goes to` api.dropboxapi.com` with a JSON body and` Content-Type: application/json` , and returns` entries` ,` cursor` and` has_more` .` /2/files/upload` goes to` content.dropboxapi.com` with its parameters in the` Dropbox-API-Arg` header and` Content-Type: application/octet-stream` , and returns` id` ,` path_display` ,` rev` and` content_hash` .


Take from it that metadata calls go to the API host with a JSON body, while anything that moves file bytes goes to the content host with its parameters in a header.


Pick the host first, because a correct request sent to the wrong one fails in a way that looks like a bad payload.


### List a folder with the Dropbox API


Send a POST to` https://api.dropboxapi.com/2/files/list_folder` with an` Authorization: Bearer` header,` Content-Type: application/json` , and a body of` {"path": ""}` . An empty string means the root of the app's scope.


If` has_more` is true, you have only part of the folder. Expect an` entries` array describing each file or folder, plus a` cursor` and that flag, and have the integration continue from the cursor rather than treat the first page as complete.


### Upload a small file with the Dropbox API


Send a POST to` https://content.dropboxapi.com/2/files/upload` with the bearer header and` Content-Type: application/octet-stream` . Put the parameters in` Dropbox-API-Arg` as JSON, for example` {"path": "/report.txt", "mode": "add"}` , and send the raw file bytes as the request body.


Back comes the stored file's` id` ,` path_display` ,` rev` and` content_hash` . Record the` id` and` rev` , since they're how you later identify which version your integration wrote.


### Upload large files with Dropbox upload sessions


For anything beyond a small file, skip the single upload call. Larger ones go through an upload session, which splits the transfer into a start, one or more appends, and a finish.


When a failure lands midway, a half-finished session is left behind, because each step is a separate request, and someone must own it and resume or discard it. Design that recovery path before you ship, not after the first stalled transfer.


Hand-writing every one of those calls is only necessary if the operation you need doesn't already exist as a ready-made step.


Activepieces has a Dropbox integration, and if the action you need is missing, you can have AI write the missing integration and keep it private to your own instance, with no vendor release to wait for.


The catalogue behind it is the 750 integrations counted directly from the` packages/pieces/community` directory of the MIT-licensed repository, roughly 60% of them contributed by the community, so you can read the Dropbox integration's source before you rely on it.
